question.problem:
The affine transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
x=5u+3v+1,\,y=3u+2v-2.
$$

Given that the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ of $T$ is

$$
u=ax-3y-8,\,v=by+cx+13,
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Reversing the action of $T,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Au+b & =x \\ Au & =x-b \\ u & ={A}^{-1}(x-b).\end{aligned}
$$

So, writing our transformation in matrix form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5u+3v+1 \\ 3u+2v-2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5u+3v \\ 3u+2v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the inverse of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2\cdot 5-3\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u} & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{-1}}\cdot ({{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}-{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x-1 \\ y+2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\cdot (x-1)+(-3)\cdot (y+2) \\ (-3)\cdot (x-1)+5\cdot (y+2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x-3y-8 \\ 5y-3x+13\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ in coordinate form is

$$
u=2x-3y-8,\,v=5y+(-3)x+13.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=2+5+(-3)=4.
$$
